taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a shrub (FEIS, Anderson 2001).

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: most plants 0.6 m to 1.5 m high, as in the photos.

traits.height_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: a shrub, up to 2 m. high.

traits.life_span.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: a shrub.

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: a shrub with spreading brittle branches.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: leaves falling in the dry season, the branches then leafless and rush-like.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: a much-branched shrub: no rosette.

traits.stem_colour.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: branches grey-green, rush-like; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.stem_hairs.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: canescent-puberulent herbage.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: leaves opposite.

traits.leaf_division.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: leaves petioled, the blades ovate: simple.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: blades ovate, entire.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: blades 8 mm to 2.5 cm long, a little longer than wide (Abrams and Ferris give their width, 5-15 mm).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: leaves suborbicular to oblong-ovate, 5-15 mm. broad.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: leaves on short petioles; 2 mm to 5 mm by eye from the photos.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: leaves suborbicular to oblong-ovate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: blades entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: canescent-puberulent herbage.

traits.inflorescence.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: flowers in naked racemes.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: Three to eight flowers to a raceme, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 152868137, 331249380, 21296914, 21784826, 19249172, 211365859, 155476067, 202272769): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flowering_position.note: Racemes at the ends of the green branches, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 152868137, 331249380, 21296914, 21784826, 19249172, 211365859, 155476067, 202272769): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_colour.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: corolla rather dull red; sRGB by eye from the photos (red to orange-red).

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: corolla strongly bilabiate.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: corolla strongly bilabiate.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: corolla tubular-funnelform.

traits.corolla_tube_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: corollas 2.5-3.5 cm. long, the lips nearly as long as the tube: the tube about half.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: corollas dull red, 2.5-3.5 cm. long.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 14, Beloperone californica: calyx lobes about 4 mm. long.

traits.stamens.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: stamens 2, exserted.

traits.stamen_exsertion.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone: stamens 2, exserted.

traits.fruit_type.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: a club-shaped capsule, as in the family.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules 1.5 cm to 2 cm long.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone californica: 1,300 to 3,500 feet, frequent on dry rocky slopes, December to May (Abrams and Ferris 1960 p. 14: February to June).

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripen from March to June.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone californica: 1,300 to 3,500 feet: about 400 m.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone californica: 1,300 to 3,500 feet: about 1,070 m.

traits.light.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone californica: dry rocky slopes, in the open.

traits.moisture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone californica: dry rocky slopes; also along washes in the photos.

traits.soil_texture.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 842), Beloperone californica: dry rocky slopes.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a rounded mound of many slender, grey-green, nearly leafless rush-like stems, a few small opposite leaves, and showers of red tubular two-lipped flowers in late winter and spring. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

generator.params.note: Set by hand for chuparosa from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of snowbrush ceanothus (ceanothus-velutinus); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.0 m tall at 10 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
